claims.source_quote_ar: وَجُعِلَ الْفِعْلُ الَّذِي بَعْدَهُ مُفَسِّرًا لَهُ
claims.claim_ar: الاسم الإشارى (مثله ذَلِكَ/كَذَلِكَ) قد يقْدِرُ له فعل محذوف، والفعل الذي يليه يُجْعَلُ مُفَسِّرًا لِمَعْنَاهُ.
claims.claim_en: The demonstrative (like ذَلِكَ/كَذَلِكَ) can have an implied (elided) verb (taqdir); the verb that follows is often made to explicate its meaning.
claims.needs_review_reason: The cited discussion in the source treats ذَلِكُمْ in a different example; applying the same taqdir-analysis to كَذَلِكَ in this ayah is plausible but not explicitly stated in the provided chunk.

claims.claim_ar: الْيَوْمَ قد يُحْسَبُ ظرفًا/حالًا متعلقًا بالفعل التالي (تُنْسَى)، أي أنه متعلق ببنية الفعل ولا يحتاج إلى جرّ أو نعت هنا.
claims.claim_en: Al-yawm can function as an adverbial/hal attached to the following verb (تُنْسَى), i.e. it is an adverbial circumstantial rather than a genitive modifier here.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source discusses the possibility of phrases being read as حال/وصف في أمثلة أخرى; there is no explicit treatment of الْيَوْمَ in S20:126 in the provided text, so the attachment to تُنسَى is inferred.
